A shabby butcher shop near Jongno 5-ga Station that specializes in domestic beef. It was so popular that it was all over Instagram at one time, but it still hasn't cooled down. I stopped by after lunch time on Monday.

They have an annex called Baekje Meat Restaurant across the street, but they seem to direct you there when the main building is full. The main building itself is not small, and I was guided by a staff member to the remaining seats inside.

The menu is divided into meat and meal items, and nine out of ten people who visit this place order the half-marbled beef and half-fried beef from the half-and-half menu. Marbled meat and raw meat are served at 250g each, enough for two people, and the price is reasonable at 53,000 won.

We finished our order by adding a bowl of beef bibimbap to the beef brisket banquet, and the typical side dishes and grill were set up. Vegetables such as king oyster mushrooms, onions, and potatoes were provided to be grilled with the brisket.

While the grill was heating up, I tasted the raw fish. It was refreshing and savory as it was mixed with thinly sliced ​​pears, leaving a hint of ice on the meat. The addition of Cheongyang pepper and egg yolk reduced the greasiness and added flavor.

Yukhoe Bibimbap is served in a stainless steel bowl with rice, red pepper paste, and lettuce, about one-third of the previous plate of yukhoe. The sweet raw meat and red pepper paste that went smoothly into the white rice were clean.

The rule of this restaurant is to spread each piece of well-grilled brisket and wrap it around the raw meat, and the combination of the heat and cold of the two was more harmonious than I expected. I wonder if the raw meat makes up for the savory taste that is lacking compared to Korean beef brisket.

reviews.text:
Personally, I think the two restaurants in Seoul that serve the best potato soup are Sampoong House and Bangadari Potato Soup.
Both restaurants use domestically produced pork bones, but the difference is that Sampoong House uses the back bone, and Bangadari Gamjaguk uses the half-bone (sacral bone).
And Bangadari Gamjagukjip is a potato soup filled with soft cabbage..^^
True to its name, gamjaguk, large potatoes are added one at a time.
The taste of this house's cabbage beetroot, which is soft and not tough, is served in such a generous amount that it fills the bowl. It's truly exquisite.
It's a magical taste that makes you want to eat cabbage beetroot again and again.. haha
Because it is boiled with half-bone bones, the soup taste is not dry or heavy... Unlike other gamjatang or bone haejangguk restaurants in the market, it does not use a gamjatang (dodaegi) made by grinding beef dashi or Miwon and other ingredients, but it is seasoned with Joseon soy sauce (soy sauce for soup), so it is not spicy and is very clean and light...
People whose tongues are accustomed to the pungent taste of food these days, who do not know the healthy taste that can clearly feel the deep flavor of these simple and clean ingredients, would be better off not coming to this restaurant.
It's a very generous restaurant where if you say you don't have enough rice or cabbage, they'll give you more.
The downside is that it closes around 4pm and you have to pay in cash only, but the taste and generous portions make up for it.^^

In Jongno, this restaurant specializes in delicious Gyeongyang-style pork cutlets that can be counted among the three main meals, and among the pork cutlets, the spinach cheese roll cutlet is by far the signature.
This is a spinach cheese roll cutlet made by rolling thin, wide pork with spinach and mozzarella cheese, coating it in breadcrumbs, and frying it. This roll cutlet is usually made in the Italian style, with soft and savory ricotta cheese added to the spinach and then fried. This restaurant uses mozzarella cheese, but the chewy texture goes well with the taste and goes well with the homemade sauce.
It seems to be run by a father and son together, and they are both very friendly.
If you look at the taste of the sauce and the appearance of the pork cutlet, it looks exactly like the Gyeongyang-style pork cutlet from an old hotel restaurant, and looking at the fact that my father is in charge of the kitchen, it looks like he used to work at the hotel restaurant.
Along with Sekkini nearby, this restaurant is the top two for the taste of Gyeongyang-style pork cutlet. Men will prefer Sekkini's Gyeongyang-style pork cutlet, and women will prefer All In's Gyeongyang-style pork cutlet.
